sentences.text: The brief facts as necessary for the disposal of the present revision petition are that respondent no. 2 got married to Vinod Kumar on 24.11.2017 at DRDO complex wherein, prior to marriage she was informed by her father inlaw Om Prakash and brother in law (Jeth i.e. Jitender @ Sonu) that her husband has qualified UGC, NET exam and is working as PGT Guest teacher in Govt. school and is preparing for Civil Services Examination.
The marriage was arranged.
On 25.06.2017 the first demand from her brother in law (i.e. Jeth Jitender) in the presence of her husband and father in law with respect to Maruti Dzire came.

On 02.07.2017, Goad Bharai-cum-Ring Ceremony-cum Sagan function took place, in which it was demanded that function should happen in AC rooms and stage should be 25 ft as functionaries of AAP are to grace the occasion.
The complaint further elaborates the demands made by the accused persons, subsequent to her marriage how the mother in law took the jewellery in her custody on the pretext that it would remain safe.

She has also alleged in her complaint that after 5-7 days of marriage her sister-in-law (Jethani) caused mental harassment and her in-laws started demanding a share in her salary, a complaint dated 27.06.2019 was filed before CAW Cell North.
On the basis of her complaint FIR u/s 498-A/406/34IPC was registered.

sentences.text: Ld. Counsel for the revisionist has argued that separation took place in 2018 and the present complaint was filed in July 2019.
It is argued that Section 406 IPC is not made out.
It is submitted that all the family members have been roped in when admittedly the sister in law (nanad) and the brother in law (Nandoi) are residing separately.
It is submitted that allegations are general and vague in nature and not even a single date has been mentioned.
It is submitted that complainant never wants to reside with the husband despite decree of petition u/s Section 9 of HMA being passed against the complainant.
4. On the other hand, Ld. Addll PP for the State submits that there is no infirmity or illegality in the order passed by the Ld. Trial court.
5. Ld. counsel for respondent no. 2 submits that the complaint is very specific, dates have been mentioned.
The sister in law was married in April 2019 the articles which were given, qua those bills were generated which have been duly verified and none of these articles have returned.

Hence,
offence u/s 406 IPC is clearly made out.
It is submitted that there is no complaint against the nandoi.
6. I have heard Ld. Counsels for the parties and perused the record.
7. Before averting to the facts of the case, the law on interlocutory order needs to be noted, as if it is found that the orders is interlocutory, the revision petition would not be maintainable.

In the landmark judgment titled as Amar Nath & Ors. Vs. State of Haryana & Anr., (1977) 4 SCC 137 the Hon'ble CR NO. 652 OF 2020 VINOD KUMAR & ORS. VS. STATE & ANR. PAGE NO. 4 Supreme Court of India discussed the meaning of interlocutory order and observed as follows:-
"The main question which falls for determination in this appeal is as to what is the connotation of the term "interlocutory order" as appearing in sub-section (2) of Section 397 which bars any revision of such an order by the High Court.

entities.text: Amar Nath & Ors. Vs. State of Haryana & Anr., (1977) 4 SCC 137
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: VINOD KUMAR & ORS. VS. STATE & ANR. PAGE NO. 4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The term "interlocutory order" is a term of well-known legal significance and does not present any serious difficulty.
It has been used in various statutes including the Code of Civil Procedure, Letters Patent of the High Courts and other like statutes.
In Webster's New World Dictionary "interlocutory" has been defined as an order other than final decision.
Decided cases have laid down that interlocutory orders to be appealable must be those which decide the rights and liabilities of the parties concerning a particular aspect.

It seems to us that the term "interlocutory order" in Section 397(2)
of the 1973 Code has been used in a restricted sense and not in any broad or artistic sense.
It merely denotes orders of a purely interim or temporary nature which do not decide or touch the important rights or the liabilities of the parties.

Any order which substantially affects the right of the accused, or decides certain rights of the parties cannot be said to be an interlocutory order so as to bar a revision to the High Court Vinod Kumar vs State on 1 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5345251/
3 against that order, because that would be against the very object which formed the basis for insertion of this particular provision in Section 397 of the 1973 Code.

entities.text: High Court Vinod Kumar vs State
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
But orders which are matters of moment and which affect or adjudicate the rights of the accused or a particular aspect of the trial cannot be said to be interlocutory order so as to be outside the purview of the revisional jurisdiction of the High Court".
8.
9.

The concept of an intermediate order was further elucidated by a three-Judge Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Madhu Limaye vs. State of Maharashtra, (1977) 4 SCC CR NO. 652 OF 2020 VINOD KUMAR & ORS. VS. STATE & ANR. PAGE NO. 5 551, laid down the following test for deciding interlocutory order:-
"An order rejecting the plea of the accused on a point which, when accepted, will conclude the particular proceeding, will surely be not an interlocutory order within the meaning of Section 397(2)."

entities.text: Madhu Limaye vs. State of Maharashtra, (1977) 4 SCC CR NO. 652 OF 2020
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: VINOD KUMAR & ORS. VS. STATE & ANR. PAGE NO. 5 551

sentences.text: 10. This decision lays down the principle that an intermediate order is one which is interlocutory in nature but when reversed, it has the effect of terminating the proceedings and thereby resulting in a final order.
Two such intermediate orders immediately come to mind - an order taking cognizance of an offence and summoning an accused and an order for framing charges.

Prima facie these orders are interlocutory in nature, but when an order taking cognizance and summoning an accused is reversed, it has the effect of terminating the proceedings against that person resulting in a final order in his or her favour.
Similarly, an order for framing of charges if reversed has the effect of discharging the accused person and resulting in a final order in his or her favour.
Therefore, an intermediate order is one which if passed in a certain way, the proceedings would terminate but if passed in another way, the proceeding would continue.
11. The present revision petition is maintainable as it is against the order of framing of charge.
12. In order to appreciate the submission of the Ld. Counsel for the revisionist, at this stage the complaint has to be taken at its face value.
In the complaint it is stated categorically as to how and when the demand was made.

It is further stated CR NO. 652 OF 2020 VINOD KUMAR & ORS. VS.
STATE & ANR. PAGE NO. 6 that demand for jewellery was raised by the mother-in-law and in order to fulfill the same gold rings to father in law , brother in law (Jeth and Devar) was given.

sentences.text: Diamond ring to husband, gold set to mother in law and 40 sets of cloths were given.

In para 6 of the complaint it is specifically stated that on the day of marriage Swift Dezire car was given after making a down payment of Rs. 1,25,000/- and remaining on installments of upto 7 years.
It is further stated that on functions and articles a sum of Rs. 26,75,501 were spent.
The complainant has also placed on record the photographs showing exchange of these goods.

She has also placed on record the bills Vinod Kumar vs State on 1 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5345251/
4 issued by the jewellers as well as the loan statement of accused.

sentences.text:
There is a specific allegation in para 8 of the complaint that entire jewellery was taken and kept in the safe custody by her parents-in-law,
the mother-in-law kept the jewellery in Pooja Room and two gold earnings and two gold rings, one pajeb and one mangal sutra was given to the husband.
In para 9 she specifically states that after 12th day of the marriage, her father-in-law asked her to contribute the amount in a committee which was to generate funds for the Nand.

13. In para 10 of the complaint it is stated that in April- May 2018 there was routine quarrel with the husband, upon which the brother-in-law Jeth started sending message in respect of court decision on divorce published in media.
Para 11 of the complaint again contains a specific allegation against Jitender as to how in September 2018, made an objection to her being employed.

14. The submission that allegations are general and vague qua the husband (Vinod Kumar),
father-in-law(Om Prakash), CR NO. 652 OF 2020 VINOD KUMAR & ORS. VS. STATE & ANR.
PAGE NO. 7 mother-in-law (Suresh Devi) and brother-in-law i.e. Jeth(Jitender Kumar) cannot be accepted as the complaint contains specific allegations with dates and year.

entities.text: VINOD KUMAR & ORS. VS. STATE & ANR
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. In so far as allegations against sister-in-law (Nand i.e. Anita), sister-in-law (Jethani Kanta) and brother-in-law (Sunny) is concerned, they are general in nature and cannot fall within the scope and ambit of Section 498-A IPC.
The order of framing of charge qua them is set aside and they are discharged, to that extent the order dated 02.09.2022 stands modified.
16. The Ld. Trial court has framed charge u/s 406 IPC only against the husband, mother-in-law and father-in-law.

She had made specific allegations in the complaint that her entire jewellery was taken away by her parents in law under the garb of keeping the same in the safe custody but was never returned, thus even on this ground I do not find any infirmity.
17. Revision petition stands partly allowed.
18. A copy of the order along with TCR be sent back to the court concerned for information and necessary action.
19. Revision file be consigned to Record Room.
